newsitem.title: USA: Washington governor unveils welfare reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Washington governor unveils welfare reform plan.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke on Tuesday unveiled a plan to replace the state's welfare system with a program that would require recipients to work and provide aid to legal immigrants.
Under Locke's plan, 60,200 people -- more than two-thirds of all those applying for assistance -- would be required to actively look for work or participate in job training.
Locke said in a statement that his program would provide both "the positive incentives and the firm hand needed to move people off welfare and into jobs."

Locke's so-called "WorkFirst" program would provide child care, health care and job training to help people find jobs. The program also adopts the five-year lifetime limit on benefits prescribed under the new federal welfare law.
Those who do not cooperate with the work requirements would be penalized with grant reductions, Locke said.
Locke said his program would provide aid to legal immigrants, who are denied eligibility for federal Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and food stamps under the new federal welfare reform law.

Locke said his budget proposal, which he plans to release next week, would include funding to serve people denied eligibility for the federal SSI benefits under the state's general assistance-unemployment program. Food stamps would also be available to legal immigrants who meet the same criteria as other residents of the state, the governor said.

"The approach I am proposing is both fair and financially sound," Locke said in the statement. "It treats people equally, and offers us the best chance in decades to attack poverty, protect our most vulnerable neighbors, and move the poor into the economic maintream."
Locke said his budget would include nearly $100 million in additional funding for child care and $7.9 million to offer work-based learning programs to low-income students.

Other components of the WorkFirst program include a requirement that able-bodied people who are unable to find employment perform community service, and a wage subsidy to employers who hire people on assistance.

Locke's welfare reform proposal would also require that teen parents participate in education programs and live with their parents or in "an approved living situation" to qualify for assistance, the governor said.
